guide: Open Start and type your agency name and your targets in the yellow cells: payment terms, target days to be paid, collection rate wanted and the write-off limit. A one-person agency can start with Invoices, Payments and Ageing.
Check Clients, Payers and Rate Card. Private pay means self-funded; a third-party payer is an insurer, a public body or an employer scheme in your area. Rates are before any tax.
Draft each invoice with the Invoice Draft Builder, then enter it on Invoices. The balance, days past due, age band, hours check and phone-first rank fill in by themselves.
Enter payments on Payments, deposits and prepayments on Deposits and Prepayments and each top-up or draw on Prepaid Ledger. Weeks of hours left and the low-balance flag fill in.
Use Ageing by Client and Ageing by Month. A/R means money owed to the agency; the share over 60 days is compared with your target.
Log every collection call on Collections Log with the promise and whether it was kept. Use Collection Priority List to see the five balances to phone first.
Enter payer claims on Payer Claims (status and amounts only). Claim Status by Payer, Resubmission List and Payer Payments follow them; the claim follow-up ranking says which to chase.
Use Agreement Hours Check to compare agreed, delivered and billed hours before you send invoices. Type the delivered hours from whatever you use to check visits; the workbook has no app and no GPS.
Use the 18 decision tools: each ends with a verdict and a what-if table. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.
Replace the demo data: delete the sample rows on each page, keep the formulas, type your own rows. A blank copy ships with the sample copy.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no per-client or per-caregiver fee, no price rise when hours grow, and your data stays with you. No macros, works in Excel and Google Sheets. Confirm tax and pay questions with your adviser.

listing.title: Home Care Agency Invoicing Excel Template: Client Invoices, Deposits, A/R Ageing, Payer Claims, Collections, Cash Forecast
listing.headline: Get paid faster for every care hour in one Excel file
listing.description:
Run client billing for a home care agency in one Excel workbook. It is built for a small non-medical agency with an owner-director, a scheduler, an office manager who does billing, caregivers and clients who pay privately (self-funded) or through a care insurer or third-party payer.

Invoices holds every invoice with its period, hours, amount, deposit applied and payment, and works out the balance, days past due, age band, an hours check against the agreed weekly hours and a phone-first rank. Invoice Lines checks each time band against your rate card. Agreement Hours Check compares agreed, delivered and billed hours per client and month. Payments, Deposits and Prepayments, Prepaid Ledger, Client Statements, Collections Log, Write-offs and Days to Pay by Month follow the money to the bank. Ageing by Client and Ageing by Month show A/R (money owed to the agency) in four buckets and the share over 60 days. Payer Claims, Claim Status by Payer, Resubmission List and Payer Payments track claims by status and amount only, with days to be paid against each payer's usual days.

18 decision tools answer weekly questions with a verdict and a what-if table: invoice draft, hours mismatch, travel and mileage charge, deposit balance, prepayment top-up, collection priority list, pause-care decision, claim check, claim follow-up ranking, short-pay recovery, payer cash forecast, write-off decision and payer mix sensitivity. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.

This is part five of the Home Care Agency Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, one flat price with no per-client or per-caregiver fee, your data stays with you, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data. It holds service types, hours, dates, rates and amounts only, never care notes, and it does not give legal, tax or employment advice. Confirm tax and pay questions with your adviser.

Payer: {col:claims.payer}. Client: {col:claims.client}. Month: {col:claims.month}. Hours: {col:claims.hours}. Billed amount: {col:claims.billed_amount}.
Submitted on {col:claims.submitted_on}. Status: {col:claims.status}. Paid amount: {col:claims.paid_amount}. Short amount: {col:claims.short_amount}.
Please confirm receipt and the expected payment date.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency and check your own local rules.

documents.title: Ageing report at a month end
paragraphs: Ageing report of {set:company} at {col:ageing_month.as_of}, dated {today}.
A/R (money owed to the agency): 0-30 days {col:ageing_month.age_0_30}, 31-60 days {col:ageing_month.age_31_60}, 61-90 days {col:ageing_month.age_61_90}, over 90 days {col:ageing_month.age_90_plus}.
Total: {col:ageing_month.total}. Over 60 days: {col:ageing_month.over60} ({col:ageing_month.over60_share} of the total, target {set:over60_target}). Check: {col:ageing_month.share_flag}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency and check your own local rules.

documents.title: Collections report for one month
paragraphs: Collections report of {set:company} for {col:days_to_pay.month}, dated {today}.

Invoices issued: {col:days_to_pay.invoices}. Invoiced: {col:days_to_pay.invoiced}. Received: {col:days_to_pay.received}. Collected share: {col:days_to_pay.collected_share} (wanted {set:collection_target}).

Days to be paid: private pay {col:days_to_pay.private_days} (3-month average {col:days_to_pay.private_avg3}), payers {col:days_to_pay.payer_days} (3-month average {col:days_to_pay.payer_avg3}). Pace: {col:days_to_pay.pay_flag}.
Prepaid balance held at the end of the month: {col:days_to_pay.prepaid_balance}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency and check your own local rules.

documents.title: Write-off record
paragraphs: Write-off record {col:writeoffs.writeoff_id} of {set:company}, dated {today}.
Invoice {col:writeoffs.invoice_id}, client {col:writeoffs.client}. Date: {col:writeoffs.date}. Amount: {col:writeoffs.amount}. Reason: {col:writeoffs.reason}.
Approved by {col:writeoffs.approved_by}. Share of the year's billing: {col:writeoffs.share_year}. Approval check: {col:writeoffs.approval_flag}. Confirm the tax treatment with your adviser.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency and check your own local rules.
